comparator.name: Law (Rechtsgeleerdheid)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 teaching and examination regulations specify 150 EC of compulsory study and 30 EC of electives. Students build from introductory Dutch law and legal skills to advanced substantive law, procedure and legal research. The 6 EC moot court and 6 EC thesis are separately required. Participation in the thesis assessment requires 120 EC including Legal Skills, and moot court requires 99 EC including Legal Skills. Professional and Personal Identity and Dutch language assessment are integrated requirements.

exception.reason: UCR offers comparative public and private law, human rights, criminal law and justice, and European, international and transnational commercial law. The available courses do not build into the sustained study of Dutch substantive and procedural law, moot court and independent legal research that defines VU’s degree.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Comparative Constitutional Law includes administrative remedies and procedural fairness. Principles of Private Law includes ownership, contract, tort, remedies and comparative legal reasoning. Criminal Law & Criminal Justice develops analysis of liability and punishment, and Transnational Business Law addresses comparative contracting and commercial disputes. European Union Law and Public International Law include digital-market rules, environmental treaties and other regulatory issues. Sustainability governance, rhetoric and empirical research add real complementary methods. Together these courses do not supply the sequence in Dutch law, litigation procedure and legal research.

candidateAssessment.label: Comparative Law, Governance and Advocacy
candidateAssessment.reason: A feasible programme builds comparative legal analysis, business law, public policy and advocacy. Its property, contract and criminal law coverage remains concentrated in broad comparative or thematic courses. Public speaking, negotiation and empirical methods complement the legal work but do not supply litigation procedure, pleading or supervised legal scholarship.

candidateAssessment.label: Law, Technology and Environmental Governance
candidateAssessment.reason: A feasible programme joins comparative and public law with climate governance. International environmental treaties, EU green and digital-market regulation and corporate AI regulation provide genuine legal or regulatory content. These topics are embedded in broader courses and do not build into a legal specialization with sustained analysis of legislation, cases and remedies.

audience.programmeDescription: VU’s Dutch-taught Law bachelor develops legal reasoning through Dutch private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law, alongside European and international law. Students interpret legal sources, analyse cases, argue in writing and speech, and complete moot court and an independent thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers relevant study in comparative law, human rights, criminal justice, European and international law, and private and business law. These courses do not provide a sustained sequence in Dutch law and procedure or the degree’s integrated training in legal research and pleading.

curriculum.limitation: The degree includes 150 EC of compulsory study and 30 EC of electives. Moot court and the thesis are separate 6 EC requirements.

componentNotes.y1-legal-skills: Includes Professional and Personal Identity 1 and the Dutch language assessment.
